g.text: Same peak, but not equally tight: 100% down to 53%
One dot: one genus starting on one night

Spawning night: one genus on one reef on one date. Percentages: share of a genus’s nights inside the white frame; an even spread would give 27%. Tight: packed into few days. Some times are approximate.

Bright pink: Pocillopora (cauliflower corals), split by sea. Shown: genera with 40+ nights, of 48 recorded. Waves are smoothed by about a day. Sunrise comes about 12 h after sunset, varying by place and season.
p < 0.001: shuffling genus labels within reefs almost never gives gaps this large, so genera differ even on one reef. Platygyra has a small new-moon peak (19% of nights). Source: Baird et al. (2021).
A genus is a group of related species. Each wave is one genus over the lunar month: higher means more nights that day.
Eleven genera peak after full moon and start in the evening. Pocillopora spawns by day, and in the Red Sea at new moon.
Most coral genera share one timetable. Pocillopora does not
